### (a) `THEOREM DOWN-SET` — and r45's `47` explained

> **`THEOREM DOWN-SET` (PROVED, mine).** If `λ` is graphic and `μ` is obtained from `λ` by
> moving ONE unit from a part of size `x` to a part of size `y` with `x ≥ y+2` (`y = 0`, a new
> part, allowed), then `μ` is graphic.
> *Proof.* Let `G` realise `λ`, `u` the vertex of degree `x`, `v` the vertex of degree `y`,
> `W := N(u) ∖ ({v} ∪ N(v))`. Since `u ∉ N(u)` and `v ∉ N(v)`,
> `|N(u) ∩ N(v)| ≤ deg v − [u ∈ N(v)]` and `|{v} ∩ N(u)| = [u ∈ N(v)]`, so
> `|W| ≥ deg u − deg v = x − y ≥ 2 > 0`. For `w ∈ W`, `G − uw + vw` is simple and realises
> `μ`. ∎

> **⛔ NOT MINE — CITE IT. `THEOREM DOWN-SET` IS KNOWN: Ruch, E. & Gutman, I., "The branching
> extent of graphs," *J. Comb. Inf. Syst. Sci.* **4** (1979), 285–295.** The statement is that the
> graphic partitions form a **down-set (ideal) in the dominance order**. Ruling: planner literature
> check `orchestration/planner_msgs/cert_w61_r48_litcheck.md`, confirmed three independent ways
> (zbMATH author query; Barrus & Guillaume, *"Upward-closed hereditary families in the dominance
> order,"* DMTCS **23**:3 (2021) #16, `arXiv:1905.09411`, which quotes it verbatim with its
> bibliography checked; and an independent 2024 re-proof, Egghe, *"The Lorenz order in graph
> theory…"*, `arXiv:2409.02937`). Adjacent unit-transfer / majorization-gap machinery is documented
> since Arikati–Peled 1994 and Li–Hu 2000, inside Mahadev–Peled 1995's threshold-graph territory.
> **The five-line surgery proof above stays as EXPOSITION and is NOT a claim.** My single-covering-move
> form (`y ≤ x−2`) is not a different theorem: `THEOREM CHAIN-STEP` below proves the covering-move
> form equivalent to the transitive-dominance form, so it IS that theorem in another presentation, and
> **a re-derivation of a known result by a shorter route is a re-derivation, not a new theorem.**
> Everything downstream (`(CHAIN)`, `THEOREM R-CLOSED`, `(DOM-MAJ)`) is unaffected in correctness;
> only the attribution of this one ingredient changes.

The proof is run **as a construction**: `G` is built, `W` is built, `w` is chosen, `G'` is
built and re-verified. **`17 278` surgeries at `N ≤ 22`, `0` failures**, and the counting

### (b) `THEOREM CHAIN-STEP`, and `(CHAIN)`

> **`THEOREM CHAIN-STEP` (PROVED, mine).** `λ ⪰ μ`, equal sums, `λ ≠ μ` ⟹ there is a partition
> `ν` with `λ ≻ ν ⪰ μ` obtained from `λ` by ONE unit down-transfer.
> *Proof.* `i := min{t : λ_t ≠ μ_t}` (so `λ_i > μ_i`), `i* := max{t ≥ i : λ_t = λ_i}`,
> `j := min{t > i* : λ_t < μ_t}`, `j** := min{t > i* : λ_t = λ_j}`; `ν := λ − e_{i*} + e_{j**}`.
> Sortedness at `i*` uses `λ_{i*} > λ_{i*+1}`, with the case `j** = i*+1` excluded because
> `λ_{i*} = λ_{j**}+1` would give `μ_{j**} > λ_{j**} = λ_{i*}−1 ≥ μ_{i*} ≥ μ_{j**}`; at `j**`
> it uses `λ_{j**−1} > λ_{j**}`. `S_t(λ) > S_t(μ)` for `i* ≤ t < j**` gives `ν ⪰ μ`, and the
> potential `Σ_t (S_t(λ) − S_t(μ))` drops by `j** − i* ≥ 1`. ∎
> **`1 021 751` equal-sum dominance pairs at `N ≤ 22`, `0` failures** of partition-hood, of
> `λ ⪰ ν ⪰ μ`, of "single unit transfer", or of the potential drop.
> **CORRUPT CONTROL: the NAIVE index choice** (first disagreement, first deficit below it)
> produces a NON-partition at **`117 103` of `1 021 751`**, smallest `(2,2) ⪰ (1,1,1,1)`.
> The `i*`/`j**` refinement is the whole lemma.

> **`(CHAIN)` (PROVED, mine).** Every equal-sum dominance pair of graphic partitions is joined
> by a chain of single-unit transfers all of whose elements are graphic.
> *Proof.* Iterate `CHAIN-STEP`; every element lies in `[B,A]`, hence is `⪯ A`, hence is
> graphic by `DOWN-SET`. ∎
> Assembled: **`75 735` pairs, `343 446` chain edges, longest chain `16` edges, and every one
> of `419 181` chain elements re-certified graphic by BOTH Erdős–Gallai AND an explicit
> realisation** (§105 — neither shares a line with the HH walk). `0` failures.
> Held-out at `N ≤ 26`: **`2 301 243` chain elements, longest chain `20`, `0` outside the
> graphic set.**

### (c) The joint walk has exactly THREE shapes

For a pair write `P_m := c_m(B) − c_m(A)`.

| shape | `P` | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `(EQ)` | `0` | `A = B` |
| `(T)` | indicator of an interval `[y+1, x−1]` | `B` is `A` with ONE unit moved DOWN, `x → y` |
| `(U)` | `[m ≥ v1+1] + [m ≥ v2+1]`, `v1 ≤ v2` | `B` is `A` with TWO units ADDED, at part-sizes `v1`, `v2` (a doubled unit on a part of size `v` is `(v1,v2) = (v,v+1)`) |

**Along the joint walks of the transfer edges: `0` states of any other shape** — `771`+`468`+
`505` of `1 744` at `N ≤ 16`, `3 324`+`2 313`+`2 571` of `8 208` at `N ≤ 20`,
`12 122`+`9 538`+`10 516` of `32 176` at `N ≤ 24`. With `d := max A`,
`max B − max A = 0/1/2` according as `v2 < d` / `v2 = d` / `v2 = d+1`, so **an INVERSION state
IS a `(U)` state with `v2 = d`, and r47's `A_j` is `v1`**. `v2 = d+1` (the `δ = 2` case the
factor-two corollary forbids) occurs **`0`** times at all three sizes.

### (d) `THEOREM R-CLOSED`

> `R := {(EQ)} ∪ {(T)} ∪ {(U) : v2 ≤ d and v1 ≤ A_{d+1}}`, where `v1 ≤ A_{d+1}` is exactly
> r47's `ρ_{v1}(A) ≥ max(A)+1`. `R` is **MEMORYLESS** — a predicate on the pair alone.

> **`THEOREM R-CLOSED` (PROVED, mine).** `(A,B) ∈ R`, `A ≠ ()`, both steps legal ⟹
> `(hh A, hh B) ∈ R`.

| case | proof | instances `16/20/22` | violations |
|---|---|---|---|
| `EQ` | the step is deterministic | `209`/`604`/`991` | `0` |
| `T`, `max A = max B` | `LEMMA T-STEP` | `332`/`1 381`/`2 631` | `0` |
| `T`, `max A = max B + 1` | `LEMMA T0-STEP` | `317`/`1 116`/`1 990` | `0` |
| `U`, `v2 = d` | `LEMMA U-EXACT` | `228`/`729`/`1 249` | `0` |
| `U`, `v2 < d` | the MARK LAW + the counting bound | `464`/`1 722`/`3 140` | `0` |
| falling outside the five | — | `0`/`0`/`0` | — |

> **`LEMMA T-STEP`.** Both sides delete a head of size `d` and lower positions `1..d`, so
> before sorting `hh(B)_t − hh(A)_t = −[t=p] + [t=q]`, `1 ≤ p < q`. The lowered entry has value
> `A_p − [p≤d]`, the raised one `A_q − [q≤d]`, and `B` sorted gives `A_p − 1 ≥ A_q + 1`, so the
> lowered exceeds the raised by `≥ 1` in each of the three index cases. Gap `1` leaves the
> multiset alone; gap `≥ 2` lowers it in dominance. ∎

> **`LEMMA T0-STEP`.** `B = A − e_0 + e_q` forces `A_1 ≤ d−1`. Then
> `hh(B)_t − hh(A)_t = [t=d] + [t=q]`: a `(U)` state with marks of value `m_d = A_d − 1` and
> `m_q = A_q − [q≤d]`. `v2 ≤ d' := max(A_1−1, A_{d+1})` in each case (for the doubled mark
> `q = d`, `B` sorted gives `A_d + 1 ≤ A_{d−1} ≤ A_1`). For `v1 ≤ A'_{d'+1}`: `v1 ≤ A_d − 1`,
> and `hh A` holds the `d` entries `A_1−1 ≥ … ≥ A_d−1`. If `A_d = 1` the conclusion is trivial;
> otherwise `d' ≤ d−1`, and `d' ≤ d−2` is immediate while `d' = d−1` forces
> `A_1 = … = A_{d+1} = d−1`, which supplies a `(d+1)`-st entry `≥ A_d − 1`. ∎

> **`LEMMA U-EXACT` — r47's `(INV-STEP′)` WITH ITS CONVERSE.** `B = A + e_0 + e_j`, both steps
> legal. Before sorting `hh(B)_t − hh(A)_t = [t=j] − [t=d+1]`, so `hh B` is `hh A` with the
> entry at `d+1` (value `A_{d+1}`) lowered and the entry at `j` (value `A_j − [j≤d]`) raised.
> `j ≥ d+2` ⟹ `B` sorted gives `A_j + 1 ≤ A_{j−1} ≤ A_{d+1}`, a DOWNWARD move; `j = d+1` ⟹ the
> two cancel; `j ≤ d` ⟹ the move is UPWARD **unless** `A_j = A_{d+1}`, where the multiset is
> unchanged. Hence **`hh A ⊴ hh B` IF AND ONLY IF `A_j ≤ A_{d+1}`**. ∎
> **`505`/`1 674`/`4 959` instances, `0` failures of the `if` and `0` of the `only if`.**
> r47 measured `355`/`1 094` with the hypothesis holding and `150`/`580` with it failing and
> called the hypothesis "EXACT on this population"; **those four numbers are reproduced here
> and the `only if` half is now a theorem, not a control.**

> **THE MARK LAW.** In a `(U)` state with `v2 < d`, `ρ_t(B) = ρ_t(A) + [t=v1+1] + [t=v2+1]`,
> and the conjugate form `conj(hh X)_t = min(ρ_{t+1}, d) + max(ρ_t − d, 0)` sends a mark on a
> part of size `v` to a mark of size `v−1` if `ρ_{v+1}(A) < d` and `v` otherwise — i.e. the
> mark drops exactly when its part is inside the block of `d` entries the step lowers.
> **`178`/`1 190`/`5 661` instances, `0` mispredictions.** Then `v2' ≤ d'` because
> `A_1 ≥ v2` always and `A_1 ≥ v2+1` when the mark does not move; and
> `#{entries of hh A ≥ v1'} ≥ ρ_{v1}(A) ≥ d+1`, which settles `v1' ≤ A'_{d'+1}` whenever
> `d' ≤ d−1`. `d' = d` forces `A_{d+1} = d`, i.e. `A = (d^k, others)` with `k ≥ d+2`, where
> `hh A = (d^{k−1−d}, (d−1)^d, others)` and the count is `k−1 + #{others ≥ v1'} ≥ d+2` because
> `A` carries a part of size exactly `v1 < d`. ∎

**Corrupt controls on `R` itself.** Dropping `v1 ≤ A_{d+1}` gives **`67`/`322`/`640`** closure
violations (smallest `(2,2,2,1,1) ⊴ (3,3,2,1,1)` — r47's own `D*` witness); dropping
`v2 ≤ max A` gives **`15`/`32`/`45`** (smallest `(1,1,1,1) ⊴ (3,1,1,1)`, r47's `(HALF-GAP)`
extremal pair). Both conjuncts are load-bearing.

### (e) `(DOM-MAJ)`

> **`(DOM-MAJ)` (PROVED).** For every equal-sum dominance pair `(A,B)` of graphic partitions,
> `μ(A) ⪰ μ(B)`.
> *Proof.* By `(CHAIN)` and the transitivity of dominance it suffices to treat one transfer
> edge. A transfer edge is a `(T)` state, hence in `R`; `R` is closed and implies
> `sum A ≤ sum B`; so `sum A^{(k)} ≤ sum B^{(k)}` for every `k`, which by `(MU)` (r47) is
> `μ(A) ⪰ μ(B)`. ∎
> Direct census: **`0` failures of `4 317` / `30 405` / `75 735`** at `N ≤ 16/20/22` with NO cap
> on the number of parts, and **`0` of `429 766`** at `N ≤ 26` on held-out code.
> Every joint state of every transfer walk lies in `R`: `2 786`/`12 242`/`24 009`, `0` outside.
> **CORRUPT CONTROL that the conclusion is not automatic: of `621 358` equal-sum pairs of
> graphic partitions that are dominance-INCOMPARABLE, `141 670` have `μ`'s that are also
> incomparable** — `μ`-dominance is a real conclusion, not a property of `μ` alone.

### (f) REFUTED THIS ROUND

**A static criterion cannot replace `R`.** `(A,B)` both GRAPHIC with `B = A + e_0 + e_j` and
`A_j > A_{d+1}` — i.e. outside `R`, with `⊴` provably dying at the next step — number
**`55` / `255` / `504`** at `N ≤ 16/20/22` (smallest `(2,2,2,1,1)`, `(3,3,2,1,1)`, `j=1`).
So **graphicness of the two partitions does NOT imply the `(U)` hypothesis**: any proof of
`(WALK-SHAPE)` had to carry information that a per-partition property does not, and `R`'s
`v1 ≤ A_{d+1}` is exactly that information. *(This kills the route "reduce `(WALK-SHAPE)` to an
Erdős–Gallai statement about `A` and `B`", which was the first thing I tried.)*

### (i) §96 — WHERE I STOP, HONESTLY

`(DOM-MAJ)` is proved and I believe the proof; what I have NOT done is get it read by anyone
else. Four specific places to attack it:

   proof here is self-contained, so priority is a citation question, not a correctness one, but
   **S1/S4 duplicate-checking on `DOWN-SET` and on `(DOM-MAJ)` itself is now owed.**

   > check ran: it **is** Ruch–Gutman 1979 (see the citation box in (a) above). `DOWN-SET` is
   > **CITED, NOT CLAIMED**. — `(DOM-MAJ)`: **no prior found, but that negative is WEAK and is NOT
   > novelty clearance** — `μ(X)` is this line's bespoke construction, so there is no term to
   > search; MathSciNet is a confirmed subscription gate for both statements. `(DOM-MAJ)` stays
   > internal and unclaimed. (r49 housekeeping, ruling `cert_w61_r48_litcheck.md`.)
2. **`THEOREM R-CLOSED`'s `U`-`flat` case is the one I would attack.** Its `d' = d` branch
   turns on `A = (d^k, others)`, `k ≥ d+2`, and on `A` carrying a part of size exactly `v1`.

### (c) `LEMMA BAND-POS` (PROVED) — `(BAND-EQ)` becomes a POSITION statement

> **`LEMMA BAND-POS` (PROVED, mine).** Let `(A,B)` be a gap-1 parent (`B = A + e_0 + e_{i₀}`
> positionally, `B` sorted, `d := A_0 ≥ 1`, `c := A_{d+1}`) carrying the band
> `A_1 = ⋯ = A_{d+1} = c` with `A_{d+2} < c` (or `d+2 = n`). Then
> **(i)** `i₀ ∉ {2, …, d+1}`; **(ii)** `i₀ = 1 ⟹` GAP1 gives `EQ`;
> **(iii)** `i₀ ≥ d+2 ⟹` `EQ` iff `A_{i₀} = c−1` iff (`i₀ = d+2` **and** `A_{d+2} = c−1`);
> **(iv)** `i₀ > d+2 ⟹ UNIT_DOWN`, always.
>
> *Proof.* (i) For `2 ≤ i₀ ≤ d+1` the position `i₀−1 ∈ [1,d]` is **not** raised, so
> `B_{i₀−1} = c` while `B_{i₀} = c+1`: `B` is not sorted. (ii) `i₀ = 1 ≤ d`, and GAP1's first row
> is `EQ` iff `A_{i₀} = c`, which the band supplies. (iii) GAP1's third row is `EQ` iff
> `c = A_{i₀}+1`; if `A_{i₀} = c−1` then `B` sorted forces `A_{i₀−1} ≥ c`, and `A_t < c` for all
> `t ≥ d+2`, so `i₀ = d+2`. (iv) then `A_{i₀} ≤ A_{d+2} ≤ c−1` with equality excluded, so
> `c ≥ A_{i₀}+2`. ∎

### (a) `THEOREM STEP-GAP-1` (PROVED, mine — corollary of r48's `THEOREM R-CLOSED`)

> **`THEOREM STEP-GAP-1`.** If `(A,B) ∈ R` (r48 §7.63 d) and `A`, `B` are both graphic,
> then `s(B) − s(A) ∈ {0,1}`, where `s` is the number of Havel–Hakimi steps.
>
> *Proof.* Induction on `s(A)`.
> **Base `A = ()`.** Then `d := max A = 0` and `A_{d+1} = 0`. `(EQ)` gives `B = ()`.
> `(T)` moves a unit out of a part of size `x ≥ 2` and `A` has none, so it cannot occur.
> `(U)` requires `v2 ≤ d = 0` and `v1 ≤ A_{d+1} = 0`, hence `v1 = v2 = 0`: `B` is `A`
> with two units added at part-size `0`, i.e. `B = (1,1)`, and `s(B) = 1`. So
> `B ∈ {(), (1,1)}` and `s(B) − s(A) ∈ {0,1}`.
> **Step `A ≠ ()`.** `R` implies `sum A ≤ sum B`, so `B ≠ ()`. Both steps are legal
> (both graphic), so `R-CLOSED` gives `(hh A, hh B) ∈ R` with both still graphic; the
> induction hypothesis gives `s(hh B) − s(hh A) ∈ {0,1}`, and `s(X) = 1 + s(hh X)` on
> both sides. ∎

**The BASE is the whole content**, and it is the half r49 did not have: `(RH)`'s
`s(A) ≤ s(B)` follows from `sum A ≤ sum B` alone, but the *upper* bound is a statement
about what `R` permits at the terminal state.

| measured | |
|---|---|
| `{B : ((),B) ∈ R}` over every partition of `N ≤ 12` | exactly **`{(), (1,1)}`**; `270` partitions in range are excluded |
| ALL-PAIRS sweep, every `(A,B)` graphic with `sum B − sum A ∈ {0,2}`, `N ≤ 16` | `33 240` ordered pairs; shapes `EQ 210` / `T 649` / `U 1 729` / `OTHER 30 652`; **`2 184` in `R`**, `s`-gap `{0: 1 200, 1: 984}`, **`0` outside `{0,1}`** |
| CONSTRUCTIVE sweep (`B` built from `A`, a different generator), `N ≤ 22` | **`13 251`** `R`-pairs, `s`-gap `{0: 7 277, 1: 5 974}`, **`0` outside**; `sum B − sum A ∈ {0,2}` fails **`0`** |
| `R`-closure re-verified on THIS implementation | `1 119` (`N ≤ 14`) and `4 112` (`N ≤ 18`) `R`-states stepped, **`0` violations** |

**The theorem has content:** among pairs NOT in `R`, `19 688` have an `s`-gap outside
`{0,1}`, spread over `−7 … 8`. **Corrupt `R`s bite.** Dropping `v1 ≤ A_{d+1}`:
**`127`** failures, smallest `A=(2,2,2,1,1)`, `B=(3,3,2,1,1)`, gap `−1`. Dropping
`v2 ≤ max A`: **`11`**, smallest `A=(1,1,1,1)`, `B=(3,1,1,1)`, gap `−1`. Both are r48's
own extremal witnesses, arriving here from a different direction.

### (b) `COROLLARY MON` (PROVED) — the four cases

With `c := T_0`, `tail := T[1:]`, `t := T_i` the raised value, `L(T) := ms(W^ε(c) ∪ tail)`:

| case | parity of `sum T` | the raise | the pair | conclusion |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **(1a)** | even | `t ≤ c−1` | `(EQ)` if `t = c−1`, else `(T)` with `x=c, y=t`; `len L' = len L` | `Δres ∈ {0,1}` |
| **(1b)** | odd | `t ≤ c−1` | `(U)` with `v1 = t`, `v2 = c−1`; `len L' = len L` | `Δres ∈ {0,1}` |
| **(2a)** | even | `t = c` | `hh(L') = L` **exactly**; `len L' = len L + 1` | `Δres = 0` |
| **(2b)** | odd | `t = c` | `(L, hh L')` is `(U)` with `v1 = v2 = c−1`; `len L' = len L + 1` | `Δres ∈ {0,1}` |

> **⭐ WHAT THE HEAD BLOCK IS FOR, finally in one sentence.** `(1b)` and `(2b)` need
> `R`'s conjunct `v1 ≤ L_{d+1}` with `v1 = c−1`. `W^−(c)` has `c+3` entries `≥ c−1`, so
> `L_0 … L_{c+2} ≥ c−1` and in particular `L_{d+1} = L_{c+1} ≥ c−1`. **That is the
> entire role of the head block on this statement**, and it is why `(UP2)` — the same
> "raise two by `1`" claim with no head block — is false.

> **CASE (2), the `467` r49 could not reach.** When the raise moves the maximum,
> `U[1:] = T − {c} = tail` *exactly*, so `L' = ms(W^{−ε}(c+1) ∪ tail)` and the two lists
> have different lengths — which is why r49's `(RH)` route could not see them. Writing
> `tail = c^a (c−1)^b ∪ rest` with `rest ≤ c−2`: at even parity
> `L' = (c+1)^2 c^{c+2+a} (c−1)^b ∪ rest`, and one HH step deletes a `(c+1)` and lowers
> the remaining `(c+1)` together with `c` of the `c`s — never reaching `rest`, since
> `1 + (c+2+a) ≥ c+1` — leaving `c^{3+a} (c−1)^{c+b} ∪ rest = L`. At odd parity the same
> step leaves `c^{4+a} (c−1)^{c−1+b} ∪ rest`, which is `L` with two `(c−1)`s raised.

**Census, `sum(T) ≤ 22`, every `(T,i)` classified BEFORE its delta is read:**

| case | instances | shapes | `Δres` histogram |
|---|---|---|---|
| (1a) | `14 518` | `EQ 1 555`, `T 12 963` | `{0: 13 264, 1: 1 254}` |
| (1b) | `10 826` | `U 10 826` | `{0: 8 966, 1: 1 860}` |
| (2a) | `3 625` | — (`hh(L') = L`) | **`{0: 3 625}`** |
| (2b) | `2 797` | `U 2 797` | `{0: 2 433, 1: 364}` |
| | **`31 766`** | **structural failures `0`** | `{0: 28 288, 1: 3 478}` = r38's histogram |

> DOWN", `219` "identical lists", `467` "not same length/sum" of `1 507`. Re-run through

### (c) ⭐ r38's `97` — an eleven-round-old refutation, EXPLAINED

`(UP2)` "raise two entries by `1` ⟹ `res(L') ≤ res(L)`" was refuted by r38 with `97`
distinct counterexamples, and the odd half of `(MON)` has carried the label
"head-block-dependent" ever since. Against `R`:

| the `97` | |
|---|---|
| lying in `R` | **`0`** — as `STEP-GAP-1` requires |
| shape not `(U)` | `0` |
| failing conjunct `v1 ≤ A_{d+1}` **only** | **`97`** |
| failing conjunct `v2 ≤ d` only, or both | **`0`** |
| on which prefixing `W^−(c)` restores `L_{d+1} ≥ c−1` | **`97` of `97`** |

**`v2 ≤ d` cannot fail here**, because `v2` is the size of a raised existing part and
`v2 ≤ max A = d` always — so the prediction that `v1 ≤ A_{d+1}` is the culprit in all
`97` is a derivation, and the run is its test.

`T ≥ 1^m` componentwise gives `f(T) ≤ f(1^m) = ⌈m/2⌉+2` by `C1-U`. Re-run here: the
ladder `1^m → T` stays sorted on `2 713` partitions (`0` failures) and `f(T) ≤ f(1^m)`
fails `0` times, strictly `436` times. End to end through `M(λ)` itself on the r29 walk:

bound attained at every `k ∈ [2,24]`, and the tightened bound `⌈k/2⌉` violated `710`
times.

> **⛔ WHAT THIS IS NOT.** `C1-S`, `C1-U` and `C1-V` are r38's, **owner-claimed and

  everything on this route is a statement about `f`, and `f` is only the right object if
  `residue(M(λ)) = f(λ[2:])`. It is measured `4 102`/`0` here and PROVED only in r38's
  own uncertified block. **I did not re-derive it and I am not treating C1-M as banked.**
